QA Test Scenarios — Import Jobs (Data Bundle Imports)

Overview

The Import Jobs page lists data-bundle import jobs (schedule/route data uploaded into the system as ZIP bundles). Administrators use it to upload a new bundle, watch import progress, inspect per-module import logs, re-run a previous import, and download the original bundle file. It lives under Admin → Import Job in the navigation.

  • Route: admin/importjob (list); admin/importjob/:id/logs (logs detail)
  • Component: ImportJobPageComponent; ImportJobLogsPageComponent
  • Migrated from: gtms-vps/src/main/webapp/app/module/admin/import-job/
  • Related dialogs: ZIP import dialog (shared); reimport dialog
  • Linked pages: Import Job Logs (admin/importjob/:id/logs)

Prerequisites

Permissions / Functionality IDs

Action Functionality ID Required role / group
View page ADMIN.BUNDLE_IMPORTS.VIEW Admin role granting bundle-imports view
Upload (Add) ADMIN.BUNDLE_IMPORTS.ADD Admin role granting bundle-imports add
Download bundle ADMIN.BUNDLE_IMPORTS.DOWNLOAD Admin role granting bundle-imports download
Reimport bundle ADMIN.BUNDLE_IMPORTS.REIMPORT Admin role granting bundle-imports reimport

Viewing logs and exporting logs require only the page View permission (no dedicated functionality ID).

Prepopulated Data

Entity Why needed How to seed
At least one completed import job Unlocks View-logs, Download, Reimport row actions Upload a data bundle via the Add flow, or use an environment with import history
A valid data-bundle ZIP file Required for Upload and to produce a job with files available Obtain a real schedule/route bundle ZIP from the data team
An import job with files available Download and Reimport actions are hidden when files are not retained Recent imports retain files; old/purged jobs may not
An import job that produced WARNING / ERROR logs Verifies coloured log rows and log-type filtering Import a bundle with known data issues

System Configuration

None specific to this page.

Dependent Modules

Self-contained; no prior module setup required beyond a bundle file.

Grid & Filter Capabilities

Common UI mechanics (sorting, pagination, auto-refresh, generic filter behaviour) are provided by the shared grid/filter framework and are not re-tested here. QA verifies that the right columns are present and that each is sortable / filterable as specified.

Use Cases

UC-01 — Upload a new data bundle

Actor: User with ADMIN.BUNDLE_IMPORTS.ADD.

Preconditions:

  • A valid data-bundle ZIP file is available locally.
  • User is on the Import Jobs list.

Trigger: User clicks the Add toolbar button.

Main success scenario:

  1. User clicks Add.
  2. The ZIP import dialog opens with title Import.
  3. User selects a bundle ZIP file.
  4. Upload starts; progress is shown.
  5. On completion the dialog closes automatically and the grid refreshes, showing the new import job.

Alternative flows:

  • 3a — Cancel: user closes the dialog before uploading → dialog closes, no job created, grid unchanged.
  • 4a — Long import: the job appears with in-progress status and progress < 100%; the 30-second auto-refresh updates status/progress over time.

Exception flows:

  • 4b — Upload rejected: the backend rejects the uploaded file → an error toast is shown; no new job appears.

Postconditions:

  • A new import job exists and is visible in the grid; the import runs server-side.

UC-02 — View import job logs

Actor: User with ADMIN.BUNDLE_IMPORTS.VIEW.

Preconditions:

  • At least one import job exists.

Trigger: User opens the row action menu and clicks View.

Main success scenario:

  1. User clicks View on a job row.
  2. The Import Job Logs page opens at admin/importjob/:id/logs.
  3. The logs grid lists per-module log entries with Created date, Module processing, Type, and Text columns.
  4. WARNING entries are shown in brown, ERROR entries in red.
  5. User clicks the back navigation to return to the list.

Alternative flows:

  • 3a — Filter by module: user applies the Module processing filter → grid shows only entries for that module.
  • 3b — Filter by log type: user applies the Type filter → grid shows only entries of the chosen log type.

Postconditions:

  • No data change; user has reviewed the import log.

UC-03 — Download the original bundle file

Actor: User with ADMIN.BUNDLE_IMPORTS.DOWNLOAD.

Preconditions:

  • A job row where the bundle files are still retained (Download action visible).

Trigger: User opens the row action menu and clicks Download.

Main success scenario:

  1. User clicks Download on a job row whose files are available.
  2. The browser downloads a ZIP named after the bundle (<bundle name>.zip).

Alternative flows:

  • 1a — Files not available: for a job whose files were purged, the Download action is not shown.

Postconditions:

  • Bundle ZIP saved locally; no server state change.

UC-04 — Reimport a previous data bundle

Actor: User with ADMIN.BUNDLE_IMPORTS.REIMPORT.

Preconditions:

  • A job row where bundle files are retained (Reimport action visible).

Trigger: User opens the row action menu and clicks Reimport.

Main success scenario:

  1. User clicks Reimport.
  2. The reimport dialog opens, pre-filled with the bundle Name; Perform autodeploy is enabled by default; Force new route version and Route cleanup type fields are shown.
  3. User adjusts options as needed and clicks Reimport.
  4. A success toast Reimport started is shown; the dialog closes and the grid refreshes.

Alternative flows:

  • 2a — Autodeploy off: user unchecks Perform autodeploy → the Force new route version and Route cleanup type fields are hidden; reimport runs without autodeploy.
  • 2b — Route cleanup chosen: with autodeploy on, user selects Cleanup unused or Cleanup all in Route cleanup type → that cleanup is applied on deploy. Default is None.
  • 3a — Cancel: user closes the dialog → no reimport, grid unchanged.

Exception flows:

  • 3b — Empty name: the Name field is cleared → the Reimport button is disabled until a non-empty name is entered.

Postconditions:

  • A new reimport job runs server-side and appears in the grid.

Notes: Legacy opened the reimport modal with the same fields. The Angular dialog disables Save on empty name (legacy had no such guard) — an allowed validation improvement.

UC-05 — Export import job logs

Actor: User with ADMIN.BUNDLE_IMPORTS.VIEW.

Preconditions:

  • On the Import Job Logs page for a job that has log entries.

Trigger: User clicks the Export toolbar button on the logs page.

Main success scenario:

  1. User (optionally) applies log filters.
  2. User clicks Export.
  3. An export job is generated for the current filter, scoped to this import job.

Exception flows:

  • 2a — No filter applied: if no filter is active, a warning toast (Export error / Filter not applied) is shown and no export is generated.

Postconditions:

  • An export job is queued; no change to import data.

UC-06 — Functional parity with legacy page (mandatory, migrated)

Actor: Any role with View permission.

Preconditions:

  • Legacy page available for side-by-side comparison: gtms-vps/src/main/webapp/app/module/admin/import-job/.
  • Same data visible on both pages.

Trigger: QA opens the migrated page and the legacy page side by side.

Main success scenario:

  1. Enumerate every legacy affordance — list columns (Created date, Name, Scheduled date, Finished date, Progress, Status, Module processed, User), Add toolbar action, row actions (View, Download, Reimport), 30s auto-refresh, logs grid columns + filters, log export, reimport modal fields.
  2. Confirm each is present on the migrated page and performs the same action.
  3. Exercise each action on the migrated page; confirm the observable outcome matches legacy.
  4. Confirm no legacy functionality is missing.

Alternative flows:

  • 2a — UI improved: legacy opened logs in an inline splitter panel; the migrated app navigates to a dedicated logs page. Functionality intact → pass.

Exception flows:

  • 2b — Missing functionality: a legacy action/column/field is absent or non-functional on the migrated page → fail; log the gap.

Postconditions:

  • Migrated page confirmed functionally equivalent to legacy (improvements allowed, nothing dropped).

UC-07 — WCAG 2.1 AA compliance (mandatory)

Actor: Any role with View permission.

Preconditions:

  • An accessibility checker available (e.g. axe DevTools, Lighthouse).

Trigger: QA audits the page for accessibility.

Main success scenario:

  1. Navigate the list page, logs page, and both dialogs using keyboard only — every interactive element is reachable via Tab and actionable via Enter/Space.
  2. Confirm a visible focus indicator on every focused element.
  3. Confirm icon-only buttons (Add, row actions, Export) expose an accessible label; all reimport-dialog inputs have associated labels.
  4. Confirm text contrast ≥ 4.5:1, UI/large-text ≥ 3:1; the WARNING/ERROR log colouring is paired with the Type column text (state not conveyed by colour alone).
  5. Confirm dynamic status/error toasts are announced.
  6. Run the automated a11y checker → zero AA violations.

Exception flows:

  • 6a — Violation found: the checker or keyboard walkthrough surfaces an AA failure → fail; log the specific criterion.

Postconditions:

  • Page passes WCAG 2.1 AA.

UC-08 — Permission denial (consolidated)

Actor: User lacking one or more bundle-imports functionality IDs.

Preconditions:

  • Test users configured with each permission individually removed.

Trigger: User navigates to the Import Jobs page with reduced permissions.

Main success scenario:

  1. Without ADMIN.BUNDLE_IMPORTS.VIEW — the page is not accessible from navigation / route is blocked.
  2. With View but without ADMIN.BUNDLE_IMPORTS.ADD — the Add toolbar button is not shown.
  3. With View but without ADMIN.BUNDLE_IMPORTS.DOWNLOAD — the Download row action is not shown.
  4. With View but without ADMIN.BUNDLE_IMPORTS.REIMPORT — the Reimport row action is not shown.

Postconditions:

  • UI affordances reflect the user's permissions; no restricted action is reachable.
